title: Audit: crypto2dev 2026-04-17
notes:
UAPI stability risk: MEDIUM — struct layouts are hole-free and 32/64-bit clean; three actionable issues: unvalidated _pad bytes in sign/verify/agree handlers (P1, blocks future ABI extension of those fields), key_fd check accepts any negative value instead of enforcing exactly -1 as documented (P2), and require_fips fd flag is not reflected in GET_STATE output (P2)
Confidence: FIPS gate coverage: 90%. Key material leak risk: 5%. UAPI stability: 95%. Details: FIPS gate coverage is 90% because every ioctl handler that touches crypto state checks ops->fips_gate before calling into wolfCrypt, and sess_free/key_free are correctly exempted (cleanup must proceed regardless of FIPS state). The 10% uncertainty is that gate coverage of provider-internal paths (individual wolfCrypt calls inside sess_init, key_import, etc.) cannot be verified statically without reading each per-algo implementation file. Key material leak risk is 5%: memzero_explicit is used consistently on all identified sensitive buffers (ioctl_init op struct, gen_iv stack IV, agree okm, inbuf, outbuf on release, key export kbuf). The small residual risk is that provider implementations (wolfssl_aes_cbc.c etc., not in scope for this audit) may have sensitive material in their ctx that only they can zero — the framework contracts require this but cannot enforce it statically. UAPI stability is 95%: all ioctl structs have explicit _pad fields with zero-rejection, algo and provider fields are NUL-terminated defensively, ioctl numbers have gaps reserved for future use, no enums or flags in UAPI. The 5% uncertainty is in struct crypto2dev_agree_op: okm[] is CRYPTO2DEV_PUBKEY_MAXLEN (256 bytes) which covers P-521, but if a caller requests okm_len > 256 bytes the validation at line 1038 catches it — this is correct but the limit is not obvious from the constant name. Gaps: (1) per-algo provider implementations (wolfssl_aes_cbc.c, wolfssl_sha256.c, etc.) were not in scope — key material handling inside each ops implementation is unverified. (2) Runtime lock ordering can only be fully verified by running lockdep. Static analysis shows no obvious deadlock (only one two-lock path: fd mutex -> registry rwlock, consistent direction), but lockdep would confirm. (3) The outbuf compaction memmove in outbuf_grow is not zeroizing the freed tail — this is correct for ciphertext/digest output (not key material) but would be wrong if the buffer held key material; confirming that outbuf never holds raw key bytes requires checking that key_export_private replaces the outbuf with its own allocation (confirmed at fd.c:1519-1527) and that outbuf is only ever populated by update()/finalize(). Would raise confidence if: (a) lockdep output from a live kernel run was available; (b) the per-algo provider source files were audited for memzero_explicit in sess_free/key_free.
